scope: Existing J02 service navigation, J03 dashboard correlation and J04 authenticated lifecycle only. No native execution, app or SDK edits, rebuild, login, publication or new experiment.

findings.claim: ServiceList and ServiceDetail explicit SwiftUI views coexist with Services and ServiceDetails custom UIKit predicate views. They have distinct identities on one RUMViewsHandler stack; whichever callback arrives last is topmost. Source alone cannot freeze native callback order or occurrence counts.
findings.assertion: Preserve both instrumentation families, every view ID and every available backend revision. Complete native callback ordering and mapper versions require separate capture; backend SDK chronology alone does not prove them. Do not merge same-name occurrences or accept owners from a name whitelist.

findings.claim: trackRUMView includes Swift typeDescription.hashValue in the view path. SwiftUI paths cannot be assumed byte-identical across processes.
findings.assertion: Any path normalization must be limited to a verified explicit-SwiftUI occurrence and its exact known name prefix plus integer hash suffix. Preserve raw values; unrelated UIKit/browser URLs remain exact. Duplicate occurrences and owner IDs are never normalized away.

findings.claim: UserMonitor.Attributes.viewName adds context key view-name. That semantic screen attribute is independent of RUM view.name/view.id ownership. Plain service selection and Back do not declare named manual actions in the audited route.
findings.assertion: Do not use context.view-name as an owner oracle or invent ServiceOpened/Back manual events. Freeze actual automatic action targets before the candidate input; named refresh/favorite actions require their corresponding declared gesture and are outside the current navigation sequence.

findings.claim: WebView RUM receiver rewrites native application/session IDs; container.view.id is injected only from lastView(before: corrected browser time, hasReplay: true). Browser view.id remains distinct.
findings.assertion: Assert exact native application/session and the browser view identity independently. Require native replay eligibility before making a container-owner claim; absence of replay eligibility is unmet coverage, not an SDK failure. Inspect no replay pixels/content.

findings.claim: Baseline ViewCache purges only during insert. An idle wait beyond the three-minute TTL does not itself evict its cached view. The candidate retains active entries and purges during lookup/insertion.
findings.assertion: J03 is an ordinary long-lived-dashboard non-regression check. It must not require the baseline to fail or claim a cache-eviction reproduction from elapsed time alone. Existing E04 defect evidence remains EXP207; no new intervention or journey is added.

findings.claim: The view handler stops the current top on background and starts the then-current top on foreground. Service detail also refreshes several data models on foreground reentry.
findings.assertion: J04 remains on the returned service list to preserve the original sequence. Bind actual pre/post occurrences and process/session continuity; do not assume the old view UUID survives, and do not treat unrelated detail-refresh action names as required.

findings.claim: The bridge replaces application/session IDs and merges ddtags, but preserves Browser source/service/sdk.version/view.id. Use a broad application/session inventory without native service or SDK filters, plus the independently complete native partition.
evidence: WebViewEventReceiver.swift: receive(rum:core:) in both frozen SDK revisions
findings.assertion: Freeze Browser identity separately from native identity. Inventory the full application/session without native service or SDK filters, retain raw event IDs and pagination, then reconcile the exact native partition. No shared service/version assumption.

finite_journeys.existing_scope: Open service list, open one existing service detail, return to list.
dependencies: Authorized authenticated app session and read-only service selection
Exact pre-input source/build/session/native-state and request inventory
finite_journeys.decisive_test: Both arms complete the same native navigation. Full backend occurrence/owner graph matches the frozen comparison contract; every accepted view has its own ID, document versions, lifecycle and source/name classification. Complete action/resource inventories retain native owner relationships; no owner-by-name substitution.
finite_journeys.remaining: Native callback order, actual auto-action names and endpoint/request inventory require qualified authenticated readiness before candidate input.

finite_journeys.existing_scope: Open one accessible dashboard, retain its native owner over the existing three-minute TTL, then one existing browser interaction.
dependencies: Native DashboardDetails owner and replay-eligibility proof
Actual browser telemetry availability and frozen interaction
finite_journeys.decisive_test: The candidate browser event retains exact application/session IDs and its own browser view ID; when replay eligible, container.view.id matches the actual still-active DashboardDetails occurrence. Compare baseline without forcing an idle-TTL failure. No captured-content validation.
finite_journeys.remaining: Runtime native/browser IDs, feature availability, timing and replay eligibility; no extra cache-purge intervention admitted.

finite_journeys.existing_scope: Background and foreground the same authenticated process after returning to service list.
dependencies: Same-process native lifecycle proof and complete backend inventory
finite_journeys.decisive_test: Native list restoration succeeds with no process restart, foreign session or stale owner. Compare complete pre/post active occurrence relationships and action/resource ownership; preserve and classify differences without relaxing the oracle.
finite_journeys.remaining: Observed native lifecycle and exact pre/post occurrence inventory.
